title: Best Over-Ear Headphones UK
short: Wireless over-ear headphones compared by noise cancelling, sound quality and battery life, from budget to premium.
intro: Over-ear headphones trade the portability of earbuds for bigger drivers, longer battery life and usually stronger noise cancelling. This guide compares headphones tested by Expert Reviews, whose reviewers say they have tested hundreds of pairs over 15 years, from budget picks to premium audiophile options.

products.name: WH-1000XM6
products.best_for: Buyers who want the strongest all-round package
products.key_spec: ANC, foldable, 30hr battery with ANC on
products.summary: Expert Reviews' overall winner. It's extremely comfortable with great noise cancelling and first-rate audio, though voice pickup on calls is only average.

products.name: Life Q30
products.best_for: Buyers who want effective ANC without paying a premium
products.summary: A long-running budget favourite with effective noise cancelling, a bumper battery life and soft earcups, though Expert Reviews notes they look cheap.

products.name: QuietComfort Ultra (Gen 2)
products.best_for: Buyers who prioritise blocking out noise above all else
products.summary: Expert Reviews rates the noise cancellation as phenomenal, with a fantastic fit and eye-catching colour options, though the build quality is underwhelming for the price.

products.name: Px8 S2
products.best_for: Buyers who want the most detailed, luxurious sound
products.summary: Incredibly detailed sound in a very comfortable, luxurious build, though its noise cancellation is only middling next to dedicated ANC specialists.

products.name: Momentum 5 Wireless
products.best_for: Buyers who want a headphone built to last, battery and all
products.key_spec: ANC, user-replaceable battery, 57hr battery with ANC on
products.summary: A crisp-sounding, impressively noise-cancelling headphone with a user-replaceable battery, so you're not stuck when the battery eventually degrades, though it's a heavy build.

products.name: AirPods Max 2
products.best_for: Apple ecosystem users who want seamless integration
products.summary: Great sound quality and effective ANC in a well-built design with the H2 chip, though battery life is mediocre compared with rivals.

products.name: Headphone (a)
products.best_for: Buyers who hate charging headphones often
products.summary: Exceptional battery life with solid ANC and engaging audio, though its spatial audio modes are disappointing.

products.name: Monitor III ANC
products.best_for: Buyers who want a distinctive look built to last
products.summary: A strong mid-range and treble sound with unbeatable durability and intuitive controls, in Marshall's classic design, though the earcups get warm.

guide.a: Over-ear headphones generally offer stronger noise cancelling, longer battery life and bigger, richer-sounding drivers, but are bulkier to carry. Earbuds are far more portable and better suited to exercise, at some cost to battery life and bass depth.

guide.q: How much does noise cancelling quality vary?
guide.a: It varies a lot. Some headphones here, like the Bose, are rated as having phenomenal ANC, while others are only middling. If blocking out noise on commutes or flights is your priority, check the specific ANC rating rather than assuming all ANC headphones perform the same.

Rechargeable batteries degrade over years of use. A model with a user-replaceable battery, like the Sennheiser Momentum 5 here, can be kept going for much longer rather than becoming e-waste once the battery weakens.

Multipoint lets a headphone stay connected to two devices at once, such as a laptop and a phone, and switch between them automatically. It's a convenience feature worth checking for if you regularly swap between devices.
